pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the plural of the English word cup? (1 mark)
   A. cups
   B. cupes
   C. cuppies
   D. cup's

2. A word bank is (1 mark)
   A. a place for money
   B. a class list of useful words on one theme
   C. a type of song
   D. a kind of poem

3. Which of these is NOT a way of building vocabulary? (1 mark)
   A. Making flashcards
   B. Keeping a word bank
   C. Using a dictionary
   D. Never looking at new words

4. What is a gallery walk in handwriting practice? (1 mark)
   A. Walking around to look at pupils' neat work on display
   B. A test of running
   C. A song
   D. A race in the field

5. Where should letters sit in a lined book? (1 mark)
   A. Under the desk
   B. Above the page
   C. Outside the margin
   D. On the base line

6. What does legible writing mean? (1 mark)
   A. Writing that can be read easily
   B. Writing with a red pen
   C. Writing in capital letters only
   D. Writing very small

7. Fluent reading needs (1 mark)
   A. only a quiet voice
   B. smooth pace, correct words and good expression
   C. only speed
   D. only loudness

8. What does reading with expression mean? (1 mark)
   A. Showing feeling in your voice as you read
   B. Reading in a flat voice
   C. Reading without stopping
   D. Reading in whispers

9. Why do we use punctuation marks? (1 mark)
   A. To make pages heavy
   B. To use up ink
   C. To hide meaning
   D. To make writing clear

10. Which question word asks about a person? (1 mark)
   A. How many
   B. When
   C. Where
   D. Who

11. Why do we put ideas in order? (1 mark)
   A. To make the story shorter
   B. To use more words
   C. So the reader can follow them
   D. To confuse the reader

12. What is a good rule for handling library books? (1 mark)
   A. Leave them outside
   B. Turn pages gently and return them on time
   C. Fold the corners
   D. Write in them

13. Which is a good way to check a proverb's meaning? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it
   B. Guess forever
   C. Ask an elder or teacher
   D. Cover it

14. Which strategy would you use to see what a newspaper article is about? (1 mark)
   A. Cutting
   B. Skimming
   C. Painting
   D. Scanning for a number

15. What is a vocabulary bank? (1 mark)
   A. A place for money
   B. A book cover
   C. A kind of poem
   D. A list of useful words on a theme

16. The cow eats grass next to the river. Which word means the same as next to? (1 mark)
   A. inside
   B. beside
   C. above
   D. under

17. What does intonation add to a poem? (1 mark)
   A. The rise and fall of the voice that shows feeling
   B. Extra pages
   C. A picture
   D. A new title

18. What should you check in a partner's story? (1 mark)
   A. Title, characters, setting, problem and ending
   B. Only the pen
   C. Only the paper colour
   D. Nothing

19. Which starting sentence would make a reader curious? (1 mark)
   A. Page one.
   B. Yes.
   C. One cloudy afternoon, Neema saw a thin dog under a tree.
   D. The end.

20. Which is a mistake in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Using a full stop
   B. Using a name
   C. Using a question
   D. Forgetting the colon after the name

21. Which line is written correctly? (1 mark)
   A. Hurray Amina: it is Saturday
   B. Amina Hurray! It is Saturday
   C. It is Saturday Amina Hurray
   D. Amina: Hurray! It is Saturday.

22. Which is the first step in writing a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Choose the theme and characters
   B. Draw the border
   C. Sign it
   D. Write the ending only

23. Which device is used mainly to take photographs? (1 mark)
   A. Radio
   B. Camera
   C. Clock
   D. Torch

24. What is a quote in news? (1 mark)
   A. The exact words of a person
   B. A price
   C. A drawing
   D. A map

25. What is news? (1 mark)
   A. Riddles
   B. Songs
   C. Old stories only
   D. Information about recent events

26. What does a signature show? (1 mark)
   A. The paper size
   B. The price of a form
   C. The colour of a pen
   D. Your own handwriting of your name confirming the information

27. Which of these is an action verb? (1 mark)
   A. is
   B. lead
   C. the
   D. very

28. What is a line in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. A whole page
   B. A stanza
   C. A book
   D. One row of words

29. Which is the correct order for washing hands? (1 mark)
   A. Wet, rub soap, rinse, dry
   B. Dry, wet, soap, rinse
   C. Soap, dry, wet, rinse
   D. Rinse, dry, wet, soap

30. What should you do to check if your instructions are clear? (1 mark)
   A. Read them backwards
   B. Tear them
   C. Hide them
   D. Ask someone to follow them

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write the verbs in this instruction: Open your book and read page ten. (2 marks)

32. Compose a short poem of four lines about caring for animals. Make two lines rhyme. (5 marks)

33. List three steps for skimming. (3 marks)

34. Plan a story that uses the proverb Many hands make light work. Give the title, characters, problem and ending. (4 marks)

35. Write a five-sentence oral paragraph about a free day. Include three interjections that show different feelings. (5 marks)

36. Explain what an instruction chart is. (2 marks)

37. Describe how a newsreader should read a weather bulletin. (4 marks)

38. Write a short telephone conversation of six lines between a pupil and a friend about homework. Use polite expressions. (5 marks)

39. Describe how to read a passage with interjections aloud. (4 marks)

40. List the verbs in: Otieno touched the handle and the water splashed. (3 marks)

41. Give the meaning of comprehension and say why it matters when we listen. (2 marks)

42. State three steps for writing a dialogue. (3 marks)

43. Explain why you should ask an elder or teacher about writing interjections in your mother tongue, and describe how to collect them. (5 marks)

44. Give three steps for telling a story fluently. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — cups
   Most English nouns add s to make the plural.

2. B — a class list of useful words on one theme
   A vocabulary bank collects words by topic.

3. D — Never looking at new words
   Ignoring new words does not build vocabulary.

4. A — Walking around to look at pupils' neat work on display
   Pupils view and comment on displayed work.

5. D — On the base line
   Letters rest on the base line.

6. A — Writing that can be read easily
   Legible means easy to read.

7. B — smooth pace, correct words and good expression
   These are the parts of fluency.

8. A — Showing feeling in your voice as you read
   Expression shows the feelings in the text.

9. D — To make writing clear
   Punctuation helps readers understand.

10. D — Who
   Who asks about people.

11. C — So the reader can follow them
   Order makes writing clear.

12. B — Turn pages gently and return them on time
   Good care keeps books usable for others.

13. C — Ask an elder or teacher
   Elders can explain the meaning.

14. B — Skimming
   You want the main idea.

15. D — A list of useful words on a theme
   A word bank stores words to learn.

16. B — beside
   Beside and next to both show the side.

17. A — The rise and fall of the voice that shows feeling
   Intonation shows meaning.

18. A — Title, characters, setting, problem and ending
   Peer review checks the elements.

19. C — One cloudy afternoon, Neema saw a thin dog under a tree.
   A specific opening makes the reader want to read on.

20. D — Forgetting the colon after the name
   The colon is needed after the name.

21. D — Amina: Hurray! It is Saturday.
   It has name, colon and words.

22. A — Choose the theme and characters
   Planning comes first.

23. B — Camera
   A camera takes photos.

24. A — The exact words of a person
   A quote repeats what someone said.

25. D — Information about recent events
   News reports what has happened.

26. D — Your own handwriting of your name confirming the information
   A signature confirms you agree.

27. B — lead
   Lead shows action.

28. D — One row of words
   Poems are written in lines.

29. A — Wet, rub soap, rinse, dry
   This is the logical order.

30. D — Ask someone to follow them
   Testing shows whether they work.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: open, read
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

32. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any four-line poem on the theme with a pair of rhyming lines, for example Feed the hen at break of day, Give her water, let her play, Kind hands keep her safe and well, That is how we care, we tell.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for theme, two marks for four lines and one mark for a rhyming pair.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read the title, read headings, read the first sentence of each paragraph, glance over the rest, say the main idea.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any suitable plan, for example Title: The Clean Compound. Characters: pupils. Problem: a dirty compound. Ending: everyone helps and it is clean quickly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part.

35. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any five sentences with three suitable interjections such as Hurray, Wow and Oops used to show joy, surprise and a mistake.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence and one mark for three suitable interjections shown correctly.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: An instruction chart is a poster that shows the steps of a task in order using short words and often pictures.
   Working / marking points: One mark for steps in order and one for a poster or pictures.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Speak clearly, keep a steady pace, use a friendly and confident tone, pause at full stops and look at the audience.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct points.

38. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any six lines with greeting, name, reason, polite words, thanks and goodbye.
   Working / marking points: One mark for greeting, one for giving names, one for the reason, one for polite words, one for thanks and goodbye.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read silently first, find the interjections, decide the feeling of each, read each with the right voice, and keep a steady pace.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: touched, splashed
   Working / marking points: One mark for each verb and one mark for ignoring the nouns.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Comprehension means understanding. It matters because we can then remember and use what we heard.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for why it matters.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Choose theme, choose characters, decide setting, write each speaker on a new line, use interjections, read aloud.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Ask because spelling and meanings must be correct and not invented. Listen to speakers, write each interjection with its feeling on a flashcard, check spelling with the teacher and sort by feeling.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the reason and three marks for collecting steps.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Know the story well, speak clearly, keep a steady pace, change your voice for characters, look at the audience, end with the lesson.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.
